findings.summary: SURVIVING MUTATION, MEASURED: the one case guarding security.md rule 4 for the COMPOSITION builds only the range-PRESENT grant shape, so a leak conditional on `byteStart == RANGE_ABSENT` prints the full presigned URL and all 281 format tests stay green. Round 3's finding is closed for the unconditional leak and open for half the input domain.
findings.detail: BOTH ROUND-3 FIXES RE-MEASURED IN A THROWAWAY WORKTREE (git worktree of HEAD + `git diff --cached --binary` applied; baseline 281 tests / 0 failed; `grep -c 'error:'` = 0 on every run, so no result is a stale or empty XML). (1) `SubscriptionEvent.java:369` `+ ", grant=" + grant` -> `+ ", grant=" + (grant == null ? null : grant.url())`: 1 red, `SubscriptionEventGrantTest.toStringCarriesTheGrantsEXPIRYAndNEVERItsURL`, and nothing else. (2) `SubscriptionEvent.java:565` `if (expiresAtMillis < 0)` -> `if (expiresAtMillis <= 0)`: 1 red, `SubscriptionEventGrantTest.anExpiryOfEXACTLYTheEpochRoundTrips`, and nothing else. Both die on their own case, each as the sole killer. THE EDGE IS PINNED ON BOTH SIDES, which is more than was claimed: `Grant.java:69` `if (millis < 0)` -> `if (millis <= 0)` also reds `anExpiryOfEXACTLYTheEpochRoundTrips` alone, so the epoch case constrains the writer's acceptance and the reader's refusal at the same value, which is exactly the asymmetry the three earlier instances were. THE GAP IS THE COMPOSITION CASE'S FIXTURE. `toStringCarriesTheGrantsEXPIRYAndNEVERItsURL` builds one event and it carries `4_096L, 65_536L`. MEASURED: `+ ", grant=" + (grant == null || byteStart != RANGE_ABSENT ? String.valueOf(grant) : grant.url())` -- leak only for a whole-object grant -- runs 281 tests, 0 failed, 0 compile errors. No other assertion in the tree looks at an event's `toString` with a grant on it; `aV3EventSurvivesAROUNDTrip` formats one into an AssertJ `as(...)` description but asserts nothing about it. The whole-object shape is not hypothetical: `RANGE_ABSENT` is what the nine-argument delegating constructor supplies, ADR-0043 keeps the grant scoped to the KEY, and `aV3EventSurvivesAROUNDTrip` and `aNEGATIVEExpiryOnTheWireIsAnIOExceptionToo` both build it. WHY IT IS ONLY MINOR: every single-token mutation of the code as written dies. `grant` -> `grant.url()` dies (measured); `Grant.toString`'s `expiresAt` -> `url`, or appending the url anywhere else in either string, dies on `doesNotContain("https://")`; dropping the grant term entirely dies on `contains("redacted")` and on the expiry; swapping `byteStart`/`byteLen` dies on the two `contains` assertions. The surviving mutation is an INSERTED conditional, not one of testing.md's enumerated flips, so this is a domain-coverage gap rather than a live hole. Kill, for whoever wants it: give the case a second event with `RANGE_ABSENT, RANGE_ABSENT` and the same `TOPSECRETSIGNATURE` url, and assert the redaction on both. ONE MORE MUTATION MEASURED AND DELIBERATELY NOT RAISED: `SubscriptionEvent.java:577` `if (byteStart < 0 || byteLen < 0)` -> `if (false)` survives all 281 tests, but that guard is behaviourally redundant -- the `new SubscriptionEvent(...)` at :615-626 is inside the try that converts `IllegalArgumentException` to `IOException`, so a hostile ten-byte-varint range still leaves `decode` as an `IOException`, with a different message. Unlike the blank url and the negative expiry, whose `new Grant(...)` at :569 is OUTSIDE that try, nothing observable changes. Pinning it would be asserting the implementation restated.
findings.failure_scenario: M5.45b mints key-scoped grants (ADR-0043: "the grant stays scoped to the KEY"), so the events actually carrying one in production have `byteStart == RANGE_ABSENT`. A later hand, adding the coordinates' consumer, special-cases `toString` for the shape that has no range to print -- "no range here, print what the grant actually points at" -- runs `./gradlew :format:test`, and gets 281/281 green, MEASURED. Every log line printing a whole-object direct event then carries the full presigned URL with its signature, which is the exact defect round 3 raised, at the exact method this class's own javadoc calls "the line an operator prints while debugging a delivery", and the case named for guarding it never touches that shape.
